text:
The Blues come in off a 3-2 win over Detroit on Monday that snapped a three-game winless run, with Pius Suter reaching 100 career goals along the way. They're missing Dillon Dube. Utah is on the second night of a back-to-back after a 5-3 loss at Vegas, where the Golden Knights won their fourth straight. The Mammoth are winless in three, and they're without Logan Cooley, Nate Schmidt and Dylan Guenther. With Cooley out, Clayton Keller has moved onto the line with Vincent Trocheck and Crouse, and Kailer Yamamoto's ice time has climbed from 13:22 to 18:13 a night.

Utah still has the better underlying numbers. At five on five, the Mammoth have taken 57% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in their games, against 50% for St. Louis, and they're stronger on the power play. They also take 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opponents. The goalie matchup favors the Blues: projected starter Joel Hofer is 6.7 goals saved above expected this season, while Karel Vejmelka is at -7.2 and has been 6.0 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. Our model has it close, 3.17 expected goals for Utah and 2.98 for St. Louis.

Keller is the one to watch for Utah: he's on a six-game point streak and has 8 points in 4 games against St. Louis. For the Blues, Robert Thomas has 6 points in 4 against Utah, and Dylan Holloway has gone eight games without a goal on 3.4 expected goals. Our under-the-radar pick is Philip Broberg, who is 49% for a point tonight, above his season pace, because his projected ice time is up to 26:09 a night.
